text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High 502/504 rate for Peregrine Health (private VPC) · observed spike from 23:07 UTC. Auto-page to on-call. :rotating_light:

sarah.ops: paging alex.oncall — can you take the lead? customer-impact shows elevated error % on ingress (NLB fronting our private pool).

alex.oncall: on it. joining. seeing 502s from edge NLB -> targets unhealthy in TG. starting handoff. tagging netops. @ryan.netops can you confirm NLB healthcheck origin IPs?

ryan.netops: quick summary: NLB health checks are flapping on target group tg-peregrine-prod. Target health show 502/timeout from targets across AZs. No config change on our side in the last 24h. Customer reported they applied SG hardening this morning.

peregrine-csm: FYI customer confirms they tightened security groups ~3h ago — said it was a compliance adjustment. They've rolled back one rule but say change set was large.

alex.oncall: ok likely SG blocked health checks. we need to validate from inside customer VPC. jordan.eng can you run the healthcheck probe from our remote-bastion in that VPC? steps below.

jordan.eng: running curl against target IPs now. output:
```
# from bastion (10.240.12.45)
curl -sS -D - https://10.0.11.23:8443/health || true
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Server: nginx

# tcp check
nc -vz 10.0.11.23 8443
Connection refused
```

mira.sre: confirming we see no connection established to app port 8443 from NLB node IPs. CloudTrail shows security group sg-0f... had a recent RevokeIngress for 0.0.0.0/0:443 replaced with smaller CIDRs. suspect health checks use ephemeral source IPs so they now get blocked.

eva.support: customer-impact: webhooks and syncs to their downstream partners failing -> ~40% of API calls returning 502 since 23:05. Customer requests a temporary workaround, low blast radius.

alex.oncall: mitigation options: (A) ask customer to widen SG to allow Redwood NLB node IPs / ELB healthcheck CIDR (if available) — fast but customer policy may reject; (B) terminate NLB -> switch to ALB for sticky healthcheck IPs — higher risk; (C) route traffic to our dedicated fallback pool in a different VPC with DNS weight shift. need quick decision.

peregrine-csm: customer will not accept broad 0.0.0.0/0 restoration. they can add a specific CIDR if we give them one. do we have a stable prefix for healthchecks?

ryan.netops: we don't control NLB node IPs in customer's VPC. healthchecks originate from NLB nodes inside their AZs — CIDRs not stable. can't give a single CIDR. That rules out option A unless customer allows internal VPC-to-VPC traffic from their NLB subnets.

jordan.eng: quick safe mitigation: create a temporary host-based accept on the app instances (iptables) to allow connections from the NLB IP range observed in CloudWatch logs — we have the recent three source IPs: 10.1.2.11, 10.1.3.22, 10.1.1.9. propose adding rules to allow those for port 8443 for 1 hour and monitor.

alex.oncall: approved. jordan, mira — coordinate with customer ops to apply iptables allow for those three IPs. we will keep this as timeboxed fix while customer prepares a SG delta that is compliant.

jordan.eng: sample commands for customer (share through support ticket):
```bash
# on app nodes (run as root)
iptables -I INPUT -p tcp -s 10.1.2.11 --dport 8443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -I INPUT -p tcp -s 10.1.3.22 --dport 8443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -I INPUT -p tcp -s 10.1.1.9  --dport 8443 -j ACCEPT
# to revert after 1h
# iptables -D INPUT -p tcp -s <ip> --dport 8443 -j ACCEPT
```

mira.sre: applying rules now via our runbook with customer approval. updating healthcheck TTL to 10s for faster validation.

eva.support: I've posted the temporary mitigation to the customer ticket and asked for confirmation that they accept iptables change. also escalated legal/compliance note.

peregrine-csm: customer approved iptables temp allow for the listed IPs with 1h window. they'll also run a reduced SG delta to add the NLB subnets (they will share subnet IDs).

incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff in 45m scheduled. alex.oncall -> mira.sre in case of escalation.

alex.oncall: monitoring metrics: 502 rate dropped from 42% -> 6% within 4 mins of rule application. some 502s remain during edge cache warmup. keeping page open.

jordan.eng: also coordinated a DNS fallback plan: if customer cannot produce SG delta, we can shift 30% traffic to our dedicated pool (rdw-dedicated-fallback) using weighted DNS. TTL is 30s. I will prepare steps but prefer to avoid unless needed.

mira.sre: logging checklist: capture tcpdump on app nodes for the 3 NLB IPs for 10m, preserve nginx error logs and target group events. tagging for postmortem.

eva.support: customer impact note saved in ticket: "Partial ingress failure for Peregrine Health due to customer SG hardening — temporary host-level allow applied to three NLB node IPs. Services degraded; webhook retries backlogged. Action items: customer to provide SG delta or accept DNS weight shift. Postmortem pending."

alex.oncall: resolution target: get customer SG delta within 1h; if not, we will proceed with weighted DNS shift and coordinated rollback window. handing off to mira.sre for ongoing ops. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
